original_value: It is hard to choose places to go from an endless number of options for some specific circumstances. Recommender systems are supposed to help us deal with these issues and make decisions that are more appropriate. The aim of this study is to recommend new venues to users according to their preferences. For this purpose, a hybrid recommendation model is proposed to integrate user-based and item-based collaborative filtering, content-based filtering together with contextual information in order to get rid of the disadvantages of each approach. Besides that, in which specific circumstances the user will like a specific venue is predicted for each user-venue pair. Moreover, threshold values determining the user’s liking toward a venue are determined separately for each user. Results are evaluated with both offline experiments (precision, recall, F-1 score) and a user study. Both the experimental evaluation with a real-world dataset and a user study of the proposed system showed improvement upon the baseline approaches.

result.paraphrase: Choosing where to go can be difficult when there are countless options in certain situations. Recommender systems are intended to help us handle these problems and make better decisions. This study aims to suggest new venues to users based on their preferences. To do so, a hybrid recommendation model is introduced that combines user-based and item-based collaborative filtering, content-based filtering, and contextual information to overcome the limitations of each method. In addition, the system predicts for each user-venue pair the conditions under which a user will like a particular venue. It also determines separate threshold values for each user to indicate their liking for a venue. The results are assessed through offline experiments using precision, recall, and F-1 score, as well as a user study. Both the real-world dataset experiments and the user study showed that the proposed system improves on baseline approaches.
